newsitem.title: UK: Seagulls instill terror at nuclear power station.
newsitem.headline: Seagulls instill terror at nuclear power station.

text.p: "The attack of the seagulls" may sound like the title a 1950s B-movie, but for the workers at a nuclear plant in the north-west of England it has become a horrifying reality.
Staff at the Heysham-2 nuclear power plant are held to ransom by the vicious seaside scavengers every time they try to make a dash from the car-park into work.

"They come at you with no warning," said Terry Mosley, industrial safety officer at the plant. "You can be strolling quite happily from your car towards the security gate, when bang...you have 20 pounds (9 kg) of angry bird flapping round your head."
So far 15 people have been attacked by the birds as they ran the car-park gauntlet, though so far no-one has been badly hurt.
Peregrine falcons were once sovereign at the plant, and used to prevent the seagulls from nesting there, but to the workers' chagrin it appears they lost the fight for residency this year.
"We'll be looking for a new deterrent from now on," Mosley said. "Perhaps we should invest in a very big cat..."
